key_insight: In the 2024–2025 U.S. influenza season, vaccine effectiveness estimates were broadly similar between prospective test-negative enrollment and EHR-based analyses.
clinical_relevance: EHR data may provide a practical, scalable way to estimate influenza vaccine effectiveness for surveillance, while generally aligning with the established prospective test-negative approach.
method: Prospectively enrolled outpatients with acute respiratory symptoms across the US Influenza Vaccine Effectiveness Network.
Used lab testing to classify influenza-positive vs influenza-negative cases and estimated VE with logistic regression.
Compared results against EHR encounters for medically attended acute respiratory illness with linked diagnosis, testing, and vaccination data.
evidence_signal: Across 6,793 prospective patients and 282,444 EHR MAARI encounters, VE estimates were 36% and 38%, respectively, with overlapping confidence intervals for most age groups.
watch_item: The age ≥65 group showed a notable discrepancy between methods, so EHR-derived estimates may need cautious interpretation in older adults.
paper_title: Comparison of Influenza Vaccine Effectiveness Estimates Using Test-Negative Prospective Enrollment and Electronic Health Record Data, United States, 2024--2025
